correctness.rationale: Uniform intrinsic-spherical direction is Gaussian mean-zero vector divided by independent chi norm; coordinate differences cancel centering. Forward/reverse maximum ordered differences F_n,B_n give exact width deficit Delta_n=2(max G-min G)-F_n-B_n. Normal extremes at b_n+a_n x with a_n=(2logn)^(-1/2) converge jointly as positive and negative independent marked Poisson processes; truncating low-mark candidates by high-probability ordered pairs justifies the noncompact maximum and unique gap. R_n/sqrt(n-1)->1 gives joint width-loss and gap limit. At one global max/min order exactly one directed root realizes full span (probability 1/2); unique limit endpoints imply simple-root angular mass tends to zero. Split-halves bound Delta_n by differences of full/half sample ranges with uniformly bounded normalized second moments, yielding mean convergence. Poisson void probability conditional on lower cloud produces constant 2(gamma_E-E log A). Independently checked exact forward/reverse support identities on 1000 continuous finite Gaussian samples; finite sampling is NOT the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Relates intrinsic mean widths and typical normal-cone exposed roots of a standard growing family. Shows a sharp second-order stochastic width loss and a nonzero mean constant despite identical first-order mean widths, and resolves the paradox that min-sphere contacting simple roots carry vanishing angular exposure mass. Nontrivial Poisson ordered-extrema law is meaningful beyond finite numerical checks.
